facts.f: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is India's central bank.
facts.e: It issues currency notes, looks after the banking system and manages money supply. The ₹1 note is issued by the Government of India.

facts.f: The RBI was set up on 1 April 1935.
facts.e: Its headquarters are in Mumbai.

facts.f: Barter means swapping goods without using money.
facts.e: For example, trading a basket of rice for a pair of sandals. Money made trading much easier.

facts.f: Saving means keeping some money aside for later.
facts.e: A piggy bank or a bank account helps you save for things you need in the future.

facts.f: Needs are things we must have, like food, water, clothes and a home. Wants are things that are nice to have.
facts.e: It is wise to pay for needs before wants.

facts.f: Interest is extra money paid for using money.
facts.e: A bank pays you interest on savings, and you pay interest when you borrow.

facts.f: Simple interest = Principal × Rate × Time ÷ 100.
facts.e: For ₹1,000 at 10% a year for 2 years, the interest is ₹200.

facts.f: Compound interest means earning interest on your interest too.
facts.e: That is why savings grow faster the longer you leave them.

facts.f: A budget is a plan for how money will be earned and spent.
facts.e: Families, schools, companies and governments all make budgets.

facts.f: Inflation means prices in general are rising over time.
facts.e: With inflation, the same amount of money buys less than before.

facts.f: GDP measures the total value of goods and services made in a country in a year.
facts.e: GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product. It shows the size of an economy.

facts.f: Economic activities are grouped into primary, secondary and tertiary sectors.
facts.e: Primary: farming and mining. Secondary: making goods. Tertiary: services like banking, teaching and transport.

facts.f: Taxes pay for roads, schools, hospitals, defence and many other public services.
facts.e: Citizens and companies pay taxes to the government.

facts.f: GST, the Goods and Services Tax, began in India on 1 July 2017.
facts.e: It replaced many different taxes with one tax system across the country.

facts.f: India's Union Budget is presented in Parliament by the Finance Minister.
facts.e: Since 2017, it has usually been presented on 1 February.

facts.f: When many people want something but there is little of it, its price usually rises.
facts.e: This is the law of supply and demand.

facts.f: The Bombay Stock Exchange, set up in 1875, is Asia's oldest stock exchange.
facts.e: Stock exchanges are places where shares of companies are bought and sold.

facts.f: A share is a small piece of ownership in a company.
facts.e: If the company does well, the value of its shares may go up.

facts.f: A debit card spends your own money from your bank account. A credit card spends borrowed money.
facts.e: Money spent with a credit card must be paid back, often with interest if paid late.

facts.f: India's coins are made at four government mints: Mumbai, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Noida.
facts.e: Many coins carry a tiny mint mark, such as a star for Hyderabad or a diamond for Mumbai.

facts.f: Paper money was first widely used in China about 1,000 years ago.
facts.e: It was easier to carry than heavy strings of coins.

facts.f: Profit = Selling Price − Cost Price.
facts.e: If you buy a pen for ₹8 and sell it for ₹10, your profit is ₹2.

facts.f: An entrepreneur is someone who starts a new business.
facts.e: Entrepreneurs take risks to turn ideas into products and services.

facts.f: Insurance protects people from big losses.
facts.e: You pay a small amount regularly, and if something bad happens, the insurer helps pay.

facts.f: Banks keep people's money safe and lend money to others.
facts.e: Banks pay interest to savers and charge interest to borrowers.

facts.f: Never share your bank PIN, password or OTP with anyone.
facts.e: Real banks never ask for your OTP or PIN on a call or message.

facts.f: Opportunity cost is what you give up when you choose one thing over another.
facts.e: If you spend your money on a toy, the opportunity cost is the book you could have bought instead.

facts.f: One rupee is equal to 100 paise.
facts.e: So 50 paise is half a rupee.

facts.f: An exchange rate tells you how much one country's money is worth in another country's money.
facts.e: Exchange rates change from day to day.

facts.f: India's financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March.
facts.e: Government accounts and budgets follow this year.

facts.f: Ration shops, or fair price shops, sell grains at low prices under the Public Distribution System.
facts.e: This helps poorer families get enough food.

facts.f: India celebrates National Consumer Day on 24 December.
facts.e: It marks the Consumer Protection Act of 1986, which protects buyers' rights.

facts.f: MRP stands for Maximum Retail Price.
facts.e: A shop cannot legally charge more than the MRP printed on a packet.

facts.f: Check the expiry date before buying packaged food.
facts.e: Food past its expiry date may not be safe to eat.

facts.f: The 'rule of 72' estimates how long money takes to double.
facts.e: Divide 72 by the yearly interest rate. At 8% a year, money doubles in about 9 years.

facts.f: Scarcity means that wants are unlimited but resources are limited.
facts.e: Because of scarcity, people have to make choices.

facts.f: A loan is money borrowed that must be paid back, usually with interest.
facts.e: Borrowing wisely means only borrowing what you can repay.

facts.f: A 20% discount on ₹500 saves you ₹100.
People earn money by working: through salaries, wages, farming or running a business.
facts.e: Money is a reward for the work and value people create.

facts.f: The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank were planned at a conference in Bretton Woods, USA, in 1944.
facts.e: They help countries with money problems and development projects.

facts.f: A cheque is a written order telling a bank to pay money from your account.
facts.e: Today, many payments are made digitally instead.
